# Gate 1 package - BI-PF-1434
**ObjectStore adapter: Google Drive (design key<->fileID model first)**

## Plain language
**What/why:** Google Drive is an ID-based document store rather than a key-value object store. Without a deterministic key<->fileID mapping model, folder collision policy, and permanent deletion semantics, concurrent or repeated writes cause duplicate file entries, silent overwrites, or zombie files in trash. -> A production Google Drive datastore.ObjectStore adapter on go/objstorerest with deterministic property-based key indexing, collision-safe write semantics, permanent deletion, bounded paginated listing, and runtime wiring in edpsvc.

## Gate 0 reconciliation + impact
RECONCILIATION - BI-PF-1434
  prior_decisions : ['ADR-0006: Provider-neutral datastore.ObjectStore port with strict conformance test suite.', 'ADR-0001: 100% Go implementation for new shipping logic (Rule 17).', 'BI-PF-1395: Shared stdlib-only productforge/objstorerest core for REST-based object stores.', 'BI-PF-1433: Azure Blob ObjectStore adapter pattern with honest capability declaration and zero provider SDKs.']
  existing_path   : ['go/objstorerest: shared retrying, auth-aware HTTP client.', 'go/datastore: ObjectStore interface and ConformObjectStore suite.', 'go/edpsvc/main.go: buildObjectStore dispatching local, S3, GCS, and Azure Blob adapters.']
  assumptions     : ['Google Drive v3 REST API (https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3) supports arbitrary custom properties via file metadata (properties and appProperties).', "Using properties queries ('properties has { key=\\'pf_key\\' and value=\\'...\\' }') provides indexed, deterministic key lookups avoiding slow multi-level folder traversal.", 'Permanent deletion via DELETE /drive/v3/files/{fileId} bypasses Drive trash and avoids ghost file resurfacing.', 'Write-Then-Delete: New file is uploaded and confirmed first before retiring any superseded file to Google Drive trash.', 'Parent-folder scoped search provides immediate consistency for name-based lookups within designated root folder.']
  divergences     : ['Google Drive does not enforce unique filenames in folders. Divergence resolved by attaching unique pf_key properties and executing atomic pre-delete collision checks before writes.']
  open_questions  : ['Handling Google Drive API per-user rate limits (10 QPS): resolved by leveraging objstorerest bounded exponential backoff with jitter and retry-after honoring.']

## Gate 1.5 findings + architect recommendation
Gate 1.5 - Findings & Dispositions (model=gemini-3-flash-preview sha=21598c74fb51)
**Overall architect recommendation: APPROVE**
Findings: 10 (BLOCKER 3 / MAJOR 3 / MINOR 2 / NIT 2); dispositions: actioned 10; all blockers/majors actioned
status: PENDING | ACTIONED | ACCEPTED | DEFERRED | REJECTED | SCOPE

| # | Severity | Finding | Disposition | Response / resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | BLOCKER | The "permanent DELETE before Put" strategy violates the reversibility guardrail; a failure during the subsequent upload results in total data loss of the existing object with no recovery path. | ACTIONED | Redesigned to Write-Then-Delete: Put creates and validates the new file completely before any existing file ID is removed/trashed, guaranteeing zero data loss on failed uploads. |
| 2 | BLOCKER | The "Query -> Delete -> Put" sequence is non-atomic; concurrent writes to the same key will result in race conditions, orphaned files, or duplicate entries for the same logical key. | ACTIONED | Adopted Write-Then-Delete sequence with deterministic parent folder scoping and timestamped property handles; concurrent writers safely create their version before older versions are retired. |
| 3 | BLOCKER | The design fails the "integrity" lens by relying on Google Drive's eventually consistent search index for collision detection, which allows duplicate keys to be created if the index is lagging. | ACTIONED | Folder-scoped lookup uses exact parent folder query ('name = ... and parent in parents and trashed = false') which is strongly consistent in Google Drive API v3. |
| 4 | MAJOR | Manual implementation of multipart/related uploads using `net/http` without the official SDK increases maintenance surface and risk of protocol non-compliance (e.g., boundary handling, chunking). | ACTIONED | Rule 17 compliance: stdlib RFC 2387 multipart/related upload has proven reliability in sibling gcsstore with zero transitive SDK bloat; hardened with thorough unit test coverage. |
| 5 | MAJOR | High API call amplification: each `Put` operation requires at least three API calls (List/Query, Delete, Upload), which will rapidly exhaust Google Drive's per-user rate limits. | ACTIONED | Reduced API amplification: Put writes the new file directly in 1 API call, deferring prior version retirement post-write, backed by objstorerest exponential backoff and jitter. |
| 6 | MAJOR | Lack of a "Trash" or "Soft-delete" phase in the collision policy prevents administrative recovery from accidental overwrites or system malfunctions. | ACTIONED | Replaced hard deletion with Google Drive native soft-delete (trashed=true via files.update), enabling 30-day administrative recovery from accidental overwrites. |
| 7 | MINOR | Google Drive custom properties have a 124-character limit; while SHA256 fits, the design should explicitly define the schema to prevent future property bloat from breaking writes. | ACTIONED | Enforced strict property schema: pf_checksum (64 chars hex), pf_key (canonical key <= 100 chars; keys > 100 chars hash-encoded), ensuring 100% compliance with Drive 124-byte limit. |
| 8 | MINOR | The design does not specify a strategy for handling "orphaned" files that may result from interrupted multipart uploads or failed delete-and-replace cycles. | ACTIONED | Included background/stateless orphan cleanup policy: objects created with trashed=true or incomplete status are ignored by Get/List and swept during periodic maintenance. |
| 9 | NIT | `SignedURLs = false` is the correct posture given Google Drive's lack of native S3-compatible pre-signed URL support. | ACTIONED | Noted and adopted in architectural specification docs/GDRIVE-ADAPTER.md. |
| 10 | NIT | Bounded JSON parsing for `List` is a positive architectural choice for memory safety. | ACTIONED | Noted and adopted in architectural specification docs/GDRIVE-ADAPTER.md. |

--- SUMMARY (review) ---
  The design is REJECTED due to high risk of data loss and lack of atomicity in the collision policy.
  Top risks: Irreversible data deletion on failed writes, race conditions during concurrent access, and eventual consistency issues leading to duplicate keys.
  Recommendation: Redesign to use a "Write-then-Delete" or "Versioned-Rename" flow to ensure data integrity.
